title: Evaluating the Role of Cancer Care Fragmentation on Breast Cancer Outcomes
text:
The receipt of breast cancer care across multiple health systems represents a significant and growing challenge
in healthcare because of potential negative impacts on cancer outcomes. This study will use health insurance
and medical record data to measure, identify predictors, and evaluate the impact of receiving breast cancer care
across multiple health systems. This research will enable the development of strategies to prospectively identify
patients with fragmented care most likely to experience poor cancer outcomes.

title: Uncovering the role for MSI2 network in hematopoietic stem cells
text:
As we age, certain changes in blood stem cells can lead to a condition called clonal hematopoiesis (CH), which
increases risks for diseases like heart disease and leukemia. This research focuses on understanding how a
specific protein network, led by MSI2, controls stem cell decisions that may protect against CH and related
cancers. By uncovering how genetic factors impact these stem cell choices, we hope to find new ways to prevent
or treat blood disorders and cancers.

title: Uncovering the Sensory Mechanisms of Blood Detection by Mosquitoes Using Innovative Genetic Approaches
text:
Vector mosquitoes transmit deadly human diseases through feeding on the blood of hosts, yet the mechanisms
they use to detect blood remain poorly understood. The proposed research will examine the diverse sensory
neurons found in the mosquito biting apparatus to characterize the impact of different cells and molecular
receptors on blood-feeding behavior. Our results will deepen our understanding of the cellular and molecular
detection mechanisms that drive mosquito blood-feeding, identifying key intervention points that could be
exploited to modulate this damaging behavior.

title: Post-Transcriptional Regulations in Stem Cell Fate Decisions
text:
Post-transcriptional regulations play essential roles in controlling gene expression in mammalian cells. In this
study, we will mechanistically characterize how key post-transcriptional regulators themselves are regulated in
controlling stem cell fate decisions.

title: Stem Cells and Aging
text:
Overall
Project Narrative
The COBRE for Stem Cells and Aging provides core services for full evaluation of cellular abnormalities in
diseases of stem cells and aging, forming a basis for therapeutic approaches. The program also supports junior
faculty with mentoring activities and pilot project support.

title: Designing germline-targeting SOSIP trimer regimens to induce bNAbs
text: Project 1 Abstract The goals of Project 1 are to design and evaluate new germline-targeting (GT) SOSIP trimers, as well as follow- on shaping and polishing trimers, with the overall aim of inducing bNAbs. The team will also be involved in the design and analysis of animal immunogenicity experiments conducted by multiple external collaborators. The outcomes of animal studies the C101 clinical trial of our prototype GT trimer, GT1.1, and follow-on clinical trials, will further guide trimer design improvements. Dr. Rogier Sanders will be the Project Leader and will direct the team based at Amsterdam University Medical Centers (AUMC). Dr. Marit van Gils will be the Co-Leader at the AUMC, That site will be funded through a sub-contract. Dr. PJ Klasse will be the Leader of a Project 1 component located at Weill Cornell Medicine. The Specific Aims are: Aim 1: To design Env trimers that can induce bNAb responses targeting the CD4bs. Given the success of GT1.1 at inducing VRC01-class memory B cells in animals and humans, a primary focus will be on SOSIP trimer variants intended to shape and polish VRC01-class B cells to become producers of fully mature bNAbs. We will also fine-tune GT1.1 to further improve its capacity to induce VRC01-class B cells when used as a priming immunogen. Increasing the initial pool of VRC01-class and non-VRC01-class memory B cells should enhance the effectiveness of the shaping and polishing steps that drive bNAb production. Another sub-aim is to redesign GT1.1 to optimize the induction of non-VRC01-class bNAb precursor B cells targeting the CD4bs, such as those of the VH1-46-derived 8ANC131-class. Aim 2: To design trimers that can induce bNAb responses targeting the V2-apex. While GT1.1 was originally designed to induce both CD4bs- and V2-apex-directed bNAb precursor B cells, its capacity to induce the latter is sub-optimal. GT1.1 binds the CH01 and PG9 germline (gl)-bNAbs but not, for example, the gl- versions of PCT64, VRC26 and PGDM1400. We will now redesign GT1.1 to better engage a wide and diverse array of V2-apex bNAb precursors. We will then design appropriate V2-apex shaping and polishing trimers. Aim 3: To design trimers that can induce bNAb responses targeting multiple epitopes. We will initially focus on generating a stable, native-like trimer that can target both CD4bs- and V2-apex directed bNAb precursor B cells. We will then create shaping and polishing trimer immunogens that can simultaneously drive the maturation of B cells against both epitope clusters. Another sub-aim is to add priming capabilities for a third bNAb epitope cluster such as the fusion peptide or the V3-N332 supersite. These goals will be facilitated by a new immunogen design, the Triple Tandem Trimer, and by applying AI-protein design methods. Finally, we will explore strategies to dampen off-target responses against irrelevant epitopes.

title: Targeting PD-1 Pathway for Functional Cure of AIDS
text:
WHO estimates that there are currently 32 million humans living with HIV/AIDS. There is a great need for
developing therapeutic approaches that acieve functional cure (long term control of HIV in the absence of
combination antiretroviral therapy). The goal of this grant is to identify a functional cure for HIV by targeting
PD-1 inhibitory pathway using anti-PD-1 antibody combined with ART and vaccination.

title: Monocyte chemoattractant Proteins and Vascular Injury
text:
The long-term goal of this proposal is to develop new novel therapies to decrease venous neointimal hyperplasia
(VNH) and subsequent venous stenosis (VS) after angioplasty of stenotic hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulae (AVFs).
End-stage kidney disease affects >4M patients globally. A well-functioning vascular access using an AVF is required
for renal replacement therapy using hemodialysis, however, 60% of AVFs require PTA to maintain vascular patency
and these fail due to the development of recurrent VS caused by VNH.

title: Transformative lightsheet microscopy techniques for subcellular imaging in physiologically relevant 3D environments
text:
Advances in lightsheet technology have spurred important discoveries in biology, both in health and disease. However,
current methods have limitations in acquisition speed, spatial resolution, and the number of possible labels that can be
imaged which restrict the types of biological questions that can be addressed. Through this proposal we will develop new
user-friendly imaging modalities that will not only improve the spatiotemporal resolution of the current state-of-the-art but
will also enable classification of 12+ different cell types in tissue that is cleared for large millimeter sized volumes.

title: Defining the molecular regulation and physiological role of a novel lysosomal mechanism of adipocyte lipolysis
text:
A central function of fat cells is to store energy when food is abundant and release energy during fasting. When
this cycle is disrupted fat tissue dysfunction and metabolic disease ensues, including diabetes mellitus. This
project will study a new molecular pathway responsible for the control of fat storage and release in adipocytes
and whether it is critical in states of metabolic stress, including fasting, obesity, and aging.

title: A novel mechanism regulating genome-wide mRNA expression in hypoxic lung disease
text:
Adaptation to hypoxia by lung cells, an important pathogenic factor in respiratory medicine, involves expression
of hundreds of genes. Our discoveries add a new dimension to signaling in this setting by showing that hypoxia
harnesses a pathway involving controlled DNA oxidation and repair to modulate the macrostructure (chromatin)
of DNA thereby orchestrating expression of hypoxia responsive genes. This research will delve into the
mechanism of the DNA structural modulation by base oxidation and repair and define its utility as a drug target
in hypoxic lug disease.

title: Longitudinal validation of retinal biomarkers against cerebral imaging in preclinical Alzheimer's disease
text:
Early identification of individuals at-risk to develop Alzheimer’s disease (AD) at the earliest pathological stages,
prior to the onset of the first clinical symptoms, holds the potential to transform the diagnosis and management
of this debilitating neurodegenerative disease, reducing disease burden on millions of patients and caregivers
worldwide. The retina can serve as a non-invasive ‘window to the brain’ and can be imaged using standard
optometry and ophthalmology techniques, allowing for screening for AD risk at routine eye exams in older adults,
and subsequent referral for more extensive AD risk evaluation. This study proposes to investigate and validate
AD risk screening biomarkers in the retina against standard brain imaging biomarkers, and then explore the utility
of combining retinal with blood biomarkers to generate an AD risk detection algorithm for cost-efficient, wide-
spread population-based screening.

title: Advanced Integration and Validation of Predictive Models for Germline Pathogenic Variant Identification
text:
This project will develop, validate, and implement a comprehensive risk assessment tool that estimate a
patient's probability of carrying a germline cancer susceptibility variant on multigene germline testing. The
model will be based on a combination of statistical approaches, building on the individual approaches of the
teams' collaborators, and will integrate data relevant to germline status, including tumor sequencing data,
ancestry, polygenic risk score, and personal and cancer family history, to predict the status of multiple genes
implicated in hereditary cancers. The resulting tool is intended for routine clinical use to guide multigene
testing, support targeted therapy decisions, and inform cancer surveillance.

title: Using Machine Learning to Understand and Predict the Difficulty of Learning to Read Individual Words from Their Features
text:
Reading difficulties have a major impact on health and quality of life with poor literacy being associated with
lack of employment opportunities, mental and physical health issues, increased incarceration rates, and
reduced civic participation. Despite decades of research, we still have limited understanding about many of the
processes involved in learning to read words, thus, we aim to provide foundational knowledge about the
sources of difficulty which make some words easier to read than others and to create new word features to aid
in future research. Knowledge of the difficulty associated with learning to read (specific) words can help
facilitate their identification for the purposes of enhancing the reading ability of young readers, and by using
machine learning to expand a database of word difficulty we aim to provide estimates of difficulty on a larger
sample of words to increase the data’s utility for educators, curriculum-developers, test-makers, and
researchers.

title: Boston HIV CTU
text:
Despite enormous progress, significant challenges remain in preventing, treating and curing HIV infection. The
Boston/Jackson/Providence HIV Clinical Trials Unit will carry out innovative clinical trials that address major
questions in HIV clinical research. The results of these studies will lead to major improvements in ways to
prevent and treat HIV and related diseases.

title: Core C: Data Management and Statistics Core
text: DATA MANAGEMENT AND STATISTICS CORE - CORE C: PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT The Data Management and Statistics Core (Core C) of the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center (JHADRC) has five overarching goals: (1) to provide database design, data management and data distribution for investigators associated with the ADRC, both within the institution and at other ADC sites, (2) to provide required data to the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (NACC), (3) to provide statistical expertise to investigators associated with the ADRC, including consultation to the Developmental Projects funded by the JHADRC and to projects of the trainees supported by the Research Education Component (REC), (4) to develop novel analytic methods for the study of ADRD, and (5) to mentor young investigators in the field. Through the provision of efficient database design and data management, Core C assures the accuracy, accessibility, and integration of data from the JHADRC. Efforts in the current cycle have modernized our database; further high-end functionality will be added in the next cycle. Through the provision of high level statistical consultation to investigators associated with the Center, a range of projects related to the JHADRC will be supported. In this cycle we add expertise in machine learning and electronic health records data to our highly experienced statistical team, and we partner to assure access to expertise in imaging and ‘omics. Through the development of novel methods for the study of ADRD, additional insights will be gained—with emphasis on methods to better evaluate cognitive decline, determine biomarker trajectories leading to ADRD onset, and enable personalized, dynamic ADRD risk prediction. Through mentoring young investigators, the next generation will be trained in statistical methods related to cognitive decline and dementia.

title: Predoctoral Training Program in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology
text: Modern biomedical technologies, including rapid single-cell and whole-tissue sequencing, high-content mass spectrometry, and modern imaging, allow systems-level analyses of complex diseases like cancer, heart disease, and diabetes. Interpreting the large and complex data sets produced by these techniques requires the use and often development of novel computational approaches. The Curriculum in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill provides the graduate training needed to develop and apply computational methods for biomedical research with the goal of developing novel therapeutic strategies for treating complex diseases.

title: InteroCANCEption - Crosstalk between cancer and the nervous system via interoception
text: Abstract Background: The diversity and precision of the nervous system enable the brain to monitor organ states via the sensory nervous system and exert control over the body via the autonomic nervous system, a process known as interoception. Nerves infiltrate cancers, where they may influence tumour progression. Notably, similar neural perturbations can lead to opposing outcomes across or within cancer types, depending on context and experimental methodology. It remains unknown when and where the nervous system acts as a constructive defence mechanism or as a destructive accomplice during cancer progression, and whether a unifying logic governs these interactions. We hypothesise that interoception underpins a fundamental organising principle by which the nervous system engages with cancer, and that distinct neurons play divergent roles in modulating the immune landscape of tumours and shaping anti-tumour immunity. Decoding this crosstalk will reveal novel therapeutic strategies. Aims: 1) To generate and validate a cross-cancer type roadmap for cancer interoception: We will functionally map neural circuits engaged by different cancers in the peripheral (WP1) and central (WP3) nervous systems. We will also reveal the neuroimmune crosstalk within the tumour microenvironment (WP2). 2) To define the neural intersection between cancer and other systemic conditions: We will define and perturb nodes of intersection between neural circuits involved in Cancer Interoception and those governing local and systemic homeostasis, including metabolic alterations (WP4) and inflammation/infection (WP5). 3) To develop novel neural modulation approaches to treat cancer: Neural modulation in cancer therapy has been mostly achieved by traditional methods with poor selectivity. Insights from this work will pave the way for new pharmacological (WP6) and neuroprosthetic (WP7) tools to fight cancer. Methods: We will use genetically engineered mouse models of lung, pancreatic, and colon cancers to dissect nervous system–tumour–immune interactions in native tissue contexts. Detailed anatomical and molecular atlases of peripheral nervous system and brain alterations during cancer progression will be generated. Using genetic, pharmacological, and neuroprosthetic tools, we will selectively perturb cancer-engaged circuits to define their roles in tumour growth, immune modulation, and systemic dysfunction—providing new, targetable mechanisms aligned with the call’s priorities. How the results of this research will be used: This work will open a new research landscape by integrating neuroscience and oncology to uncover how neural circuits regulate cancer and systemic homeostasis. It will deliver broadly applicable tools and establish more selective neuromodulation as new cancer therapeutic avenues that synergise with existing ones.

title: A generalizable computational platform for early organ vulnerability modeling and therapeutic discovery using systemic omics and imaging
text:
This project will develop a computational platform that integrates imaging, omics, and genetic data to
identify early, spatially localized tissue vulnerability and discover therapeutic strategies through drug
repurposing. By enabling personalized risk prediction and intervention across multiple organs, this
work will advance precision medicine and improve outcomes for common chronic diseases.

title: Novel Dual Agent HP C-13 MRI for Quantitative Imaging of Prostate Cancer Aggressiveness for Improved Biopsy Guidance
text:
The goal of this project is to develop novel techniques for a novel dual-contrast agent MR molecular imaging
approach to simultaneously detect HP pyruvate metabolism and urea tissue-perfusion in prostate cancer patients
for detecting aggressive cancers and to direct “biomarker-driven” guided fusion biopsies for the first time.
Although this study focuses on prostate cancer and a novel investigational contrast-agent combination, these
methods are applicable widely to other investigations of different cancers and diseases.
